title: Starfall
description: The card-#88 demo game: a starfield shooter drawn in the SCREEN, SPRITES and PALETTES panels, played with the pad, split by the raster table and scored in sprites.

-- main.lua — STARFALL, a small game made only in the studio (card #88).
--
-- WHAT THIS PROVES: a person with the studio's code editor, its SCREEN,
-- SPRITES and PALETTES panels, its toy runtime and its pad can make a game
-- that runs in the browser — and the same file runs through the IL interpreter
-- (the Lua / IL switch in the transport), so it is already inside the path
-- the console back end takes.
--
-- THE GAME: six drones fall through a scrolling starfield.  Move with the
-- D-pad, fire with I.  A hit scores; a collision costs a life.  The top 24
-- lines are a status bar: the RCR line interrupt keeps them still (BYR 0) and
-- a shade darker while the playfield below scrolls (BYR = scroll), which is
-- the raster table's own demonstration.  Score and lives are sprites, because
-- the BAT scrolls under them.
--
-- HOW THE ART GOT HERE: tiles.json / palettes.json / sprites.json in this
-- folder are the picture the SCREEN, SPRITES and PALETTES panels edit.  A toy
-- cannot read those files (there is no asset importer yet — card #117 — see
-- the README's shortfalls), so tools/demo-game-assets.js writes the panels'
-- picture into the block below between the two markers.  Edit the panels, run
--
--     node tools/demo-game-assets.js
--
-- and the block is rewritten; the hand-written game below it is untouched.
-- The generator refuses to run if the markers are gone.
--
-- WHAT IT COULD NOT USE: the card asks for the hardware's collision flags and
-- for toy sound.  A toy cannot read SR (CC/OR) at all (#119), so collisions
-- are arithmetic; and sfx() with no music() is master-muted (#113), so the
-- game's sound writes PSG events that fall silent — the README lists both.
-- The entity lists and the HUD digits are spelled out because the IL refuses
-- to read a table index (#118).
--
-- Everything between the markers is generated: do not edit it by hand.

-- >>> PCEStudio demo art — generated by tools/demo-game-assets.js; do not edit

-- toy's own VRAM and CRAM.  There is no asset importer yet (#117);
-- block is the bridge.  Edit the panels, then run the tool.

-- The game's state lives in globals, one per value instead of an array:
-- the IL's tables are write-only (il-table-read, card #118), so `b[0].x`
-- cannot exist.  That is a shortfall of the toy language this game had to work
-- around; see the README.
--
-- Sprite slots (the SAT):
--   0..2  score digits, hundreds/tens/ones   3..5  lives
--   6     player                             7..12 enemies
--   13..16 bullets
--
-- The pattern numbers (SHIP, ENEMY, BULLET, HEART, DIGIT_*), the starting
-- positions (START_PX, E0X0..) and the two bar colours come from the
-- generated block above, so the picture the panels show and the game's first
-- frame are one source.

function reset_bullet(n)
  if n == 0 then b0l = 0 elseif n == 1 then b1l = 0
  elseif n == 2 then b2l = 0 else b3l = 0 end
end

-- A free bullet leaves from the ship's nose.  No array: four slots, spelled.
function fire()
  if b0l == 0 then
    b0l = 1 b0x = px + 7 b0y = py - 2
  elseif b1l == 0 then
    b1l = 1 b1x = px + 7 b1y = py - 2
  elseif b2l == 0 then
    b2l = 1 b2x = px + 7 b2y = py - 2
  elseif b3l == 0 then
    b3l = 1 b3x = px + 7 b3y = py - 2
  end
end

-- The spawn x for an enemy that left the screen.  A tiny LCG whose product
-- stays inside 32 bits, so Lua and the IL's wrapping int agree by
-- construction: 250 * 37 + 101 < 2^31.
function rnd()
  rng = (rng * 37 + 101) % 251
  return rng
end

-- A 16x16 sprite's box against another: the cell's own coordinates, no
-- hardware status register (a toy cannot read the VDC's CC/OR flags — card
-- #119 — see the README).
function hit(ax, ay, bx, by)
  if abs(ax - bx) < 12 then
    if abs(ay - by) < 12 then return 1 end
  end
  return 0
end

function lose_life()
  lives = lives - 1
  inv = 90
  sfx(2, 220, 20, 16)
  if lives <= 0 then
    lives = 3
    score = 0
  end
end

function init()
  -- the panels' picture: palettes, tiles, the BAT and the sprite patterns
  art_boot()
  -- the SAT as the SPRITES panel shows it: the start state of every slot
  art_sat()

  -- BB (background) and SB (sprites) on.  The toy host starts at BB only
  -- (card #120), so a toy that forgets this draws a SAT nobody can see.
  reg("CR", 0xC0)

  -- The status bar: line 0 freezes the scroll and darkens the backdrop; line
  -- 24 (set every frame) releases the scroll to `scroll` and restores the
  -- backdrop.  The bar is 24 lines, three tile rows.
  raster(0, {byr = 0, cram = {{0, C_BAR}}})

  px = START_PX
  py = START_PY
  lives = 3
  score = 0
  inv = 90
  cooldown = 0
  scroll = 0
  rng = 3

  b0l = 0 b0x = 0 b0y = 0
  b1l = 0 b1x = 0 b1y = 0
  b2l = 0 b2x = 0 b2y = 0
  b3l = 0 b3x = 0 b3y = 0

  ex0 = E0X0 ey0 = E0Y0 es0 = 1
  ex1 = E1X0 ey1 = E1Y0 es1 = 2
  ex2 = E2X0 ey2 = E2Y0 es2 = 1
  ex3 = E3X0 ey3 = E3Y0 es3 = 2
  ex4 = E4X0 ey4 = E4Y0 es4 = 1
  ex5 = E5X0 ey5 = E5Y0 es5 = 1
end

-- Bullets: up four pixels a frame, gone above the bar.
function move_bullets()
  if b0l == 1 then
    b0y = b0y - 4
    if b0y < 26 then b0l = 0 end
  end
  if b1l == 1 then
    b1y = b1y - 4
    if b1y < 26 then b1l = 0 end
  end
  if b2l == 1 then
    b2y = b2y - 4
    if b2y < 26 then b2l = 0 end
  end
  if b3l == 1 then
    b3y = b3y - 4
    if b3y < 26 then b3l = 0 end
  end
end

-- Enemies: down at their own speed, and a hit or a wrap sends them back to
-- the top at a new x.  Six slots, six blocks; there is no loop over the
-- entities because there is no way to index them.
function move_enemies()
  ey0 = ey0 + es0
  if ey0 > 232 then ey0 = 24 ex0 = rnd() % 224 end
  ey1 = ey1 + es1

function touch_player()
  if inv > 0 then
    inv = inv - 1
  else
    if hit(px, py, ex0, ey0) == 1 then lose_life()
    elseif hit(px, py, ex1, ey1) == 1 then lose_life()
    elseif hit(px, py, ex2, ey2) == 1 then lose_life()
    elseif hit(px, py, ex3, ey3) == 1 then lose_life()
    elseif hit(px, py, ex4, ey4) == 1 then lose_life()
    elseif hit(px, py, ex5, ey5) == 1 then lose_life()
    end
  end
end

-- One digit's pattern for a score digit.  The ten pattern codes sit in VRAM
-- at DIGIT_BASE and are read back with vram[], because a table of ten numbers
-- cannot be read in the IL (il-table-read) and a ten-way if would bury the
-- logic.  VRAM is the one array both runtimes can read.
function digit_pattern(d)
  return vram[DIGIT_BASE + d]
end

-- The HUD.  Score on the right, lives on the left; both are sprites, so the
-- scrolling BAT below cannot carry them.
function draw_hud()
  local d1 = (score // 100) % 10
  local d2 = (score // 10) % 10
  local d3 = score % 10
  sprite(0, {x = 196, y = 68, pattern = digit_pattern(d1), palette = 1})
  sprite(1, {x = 210, y = 68, pattern = digit_pattern(d2), palette = 1})
  sprite(2, {x = 224, y = 68, pattern = digit_pattern(d3), palette = 1})
  if lives >= 1 then
    sprite(3, {x = 8, y = 68, pattern = HEART, palette = 1})
  else
    sprite(3, {y = 0})
  end
  if lives >= 2 then
    sprite(4, {x = 24, y = 68, pattern = HEART, palette = 1})
  else
    sprite(4, {y = 0})
  end
  if lives >= 3 then
    sprite(5, {x = 40, y = 68, pattern = HEART, palette = 1})
  else
    sprite(5, {y = 0})
  end
end

function draw_ship()
  -- a hit flashes the ship off for two frames out of four while inv runs down
  local flash = 0
  if inv > 0 then
    if (inv // 4) % 2 == 0 then flash = 1 end
  end
  if flash == 1 then
    sprite(6, {y = 0})
  else
    sprite(6, {x = px, y = py + 64, pattern = SHIP, palette = 0})
  end
end

function frame(t, f)
  -- the starfield: one pixel a frame, wrapping at the 32-row BAT's 256 lines
  scroll = (scroll + 1) % 256
  reg("BYR", 0)

  -- The RCR split, from the raster table: line 24 releases the scroll and the
  -- playfield's backdrop.  Re-registered every frame because the offset moves.
  raster(24, {byr = scroll, cram = {{0, C_FIELD}}})

  -- pad[1]: the studio's IJKL/NM/OP keys, and the scripted pad in the test
  if pad[1].left then px = px - 2 end
  if pad[1].right then px = px + 2 end
  if pad[1].up then py = py - 2 end
  if pad[1].down then py = py + 2 end
  if px < 0 then px = 0 end
  if px > 240 then px = 240 end
  if py < 34 then py = 34 end
  if py > 200 then py = 200 end

  if cooldown > 0 then cooldown = cooldown - 1 end
  if pad[1].i then
    if cooldown == 0 then
      fire()
      cooldown = 8
      sfx(0, 1100, 14, 4)
    end
  end

  move_bullets()
  move_enemies()
  collide()
  touch_player()

  draw_hud()
  draw_ship()
  draw_bullets()
  draw_enemies()
end
